title: Laser Squad
build: Blade Software's 48K tape (TOSEC: Laser Squad (1988)(Blade)[scenario 1-2].tzx and [scenario 3-5].tzx): a BASIC loader, the loading screen, the 22,521-byte engine at $5E28-$B620 and five headerless scenario blocks of 18,911 bytes each, loaded at $B621-$FFFF

records.c: The hook for the computer's half-turn, which the engine calls in place of a player's (halfTurn at $5F4E): a jump to aiTurn ($B89B).
The hook for the computer's fire: its units' shots in its own turn (peek) and their reaction when an enemy moves in their sight (startReaction, $755D): a jump to aiFire ($BF29).
The hook for the square a shot has reached ($7091): a jump to shotSeen ($C177).
The hook for the computer's turn on the screen: called as it begins, for each of its units and at each step one makes: a jump to hideView ($C213).
The hook for a step about to be made, its square at $5D3E: a RET, as this scenario adds nothing there.
The two bytes after scenarioStep's RET, $00 $00: the room for a jump's address, unused here.
The hook for the end of each half-turn ($5F7B): a jump to cyberReinforce ($FF67).
The hook for a unit's menu, just built: a RET, as this scenario adds nothing there.
The two bytes after scenarioMenu's RET, $00 $00: the room for a jump's address, unused here.
The hook for the scenario's own option, $0D, chosen from a unit's menu: a RET, as this scenario adds nothing there.
The two bytes after scenarioOption's RET, $00 $00: the room for a jump's address, unused here.
The number of the scenario's objects at the start: 100, listed at objects ($D068).

The computer's memory of each unit, $8C to $9F, a byte each: when an enemy is seen or heard firing it is set to the computer's skill ($5DF8), and it goes down by one in each of the first side's half-turns ($5EB8). An enemy is hunted while its count is not 0.
The tiles of a blow in close combat (blowOnScreen, $7F98), drawn in turn over the square: $AE, $AD, $AC, $AB, ended by $FF.
The two tiles of a hit by a shot ($8371), $84 and $85, drawn over the square in yellow for every four points of damage.
The computer's skill at each level, 1 to 7 (into $5DF8, which sets how long it remembers an enemy): 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. This scenario has 7 levels.
The victory points for wiping out a side ($A4A4): 100 to the second side when the first has no units left, 100 to the first when the second has none.

The squares for placing units (placeUnits, $A370), six of three bytes: the code on the map, the side whose squares they are, and the floor the code stands for, put back when the placing is over ($A474): $3B for side 0 over $01; $3A for side 1 over $1A; $FF for side 255 over $FF; $FF for side 255 over $FF; $FF for side 255 over $FF; $FF for side 255 over $FF.

Which units play in each mode, a byte for each unit $8C to $9F: bit 0 for a game of two players, bit n for level n against the computer ($A2BA): $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FF $FD $F9 $FF $FF $F1 $81 $FF $FC $F0 $C0.
The number of levels against the computer: 7 (message $5F asks for one).

The first side's price list in the shop ($9D55), a byte for each kind of object $6E to $8B, $FF for one not for sale: Marsec Auto-Gun 14; Heavy Laser 17; M50 Auto Pistol 8; L80 Las-Gun 10; Pump Shot Gun 8; Ms Auto Cannon 18; Mk-1 22; Ap50 Grenade 4; Ap75 Grenade 7; Light Sabre 4; Marsec Gun Clip 2; Heavy Las-Pack 5; Pistol Clip 1; L80 Las-Pack 2; Shot Gun Clip 1; Cannon Clip 5; Mk-1 Clip 6.

The second side's price list in the shop ($9D55), a byte for each kind of object $6E to $8B, $FF for one not for sale: Marsec Auto-Gun 17; Heavy Laser 21; M50 Auto Pistol 10; L80 Las-Gun 12; Pump Shot Gun 10; Ms Auto Cannon 20; Marsec Gun Clip 3; Heavy Las-Pack 6; Pistol Clip 2; L80 Las-Pack 2; Shot Gun Clip 2; Cannon Clip 8.

The five types of armour, seven bytes each ($9EAB): the armour at the front, left, right and rear, its cost in action points each turn ($11), the room it leaves to carry ($26), and its price. type 0: front 0, left 0, right 0, rear 0, 0 a turn, room 110, price 0; type 1: front 15, left 12, right 12, rear 10, 1 a turn, room 90, price 5; type 2: front 22, left 17, right 17, rear 14, 2 a turn, room 80, price 8; type 3: front 30, left 25, right 25, rear 20, 4 a turn, room 70, price 11; type 4: front 38, left 31, right 31, rear 27, 7 a turn, room 60, price 15.

Each unit's flags, $8C to $9F: bit 0 equipped in the first side's shop ($9E50), bit 1 in the second side's, bit 2 placed by its side's player ($A370) rather than arriving at random in its patch ($A2EE): $05 $05 $05 $05 $05 $05 $05 $05 $06 $06 $06 $06 $04 $04 $04 $04 $04 $04 $04 $04.
Each side's credits for the shop: 255 and 100 at the start, the first side's set by the level against the computer.
The first side's credits at each level against the computer, 1 to 7 ($A211): 250, 230, 210, 190, 170, 150, 130.
The last turn: 70. The game ends when it has been played ($A4A4).
The colours of each side's name on the bottom line ($6785): $44 and $45.
Who scores for damage to the terrain ($9201): the first side when the first byte is set (0), the second when the second is (1).
Set in a game against the computer, which has the second side.
Each side's view and cursor, four bytes a side ($5FA7): the map's row and column at the view's top left, and the cursor's row and column in the view.
The side whose half-turn it is: 0 the first, 1 the second.
An enemy unit the computer goes after: the one knownEnemy found, or the one that moved into sight before a reaction ($755D).
Set when the computer has been alerted: an enemy seen, a shot seen, an explosion ($9696). With it set, units whose orders allow it keep half their action points in hand.
Set while the view is blanked in the computer's turn (hideView); drawView clears it.
The table of squares drawView draws through: squares ($E65F) in play, fireSquares ($E79F) in fire mode.
The cursor's last row and column in the view ($635C, $63C0): 10 in play, $A7 in fire mode, where the cursor moves by pixels.
The cursor's first row and column in the view ($6380, $63A0): 0 in play, 8 in fire mode.
The cursor's blink, counted down: 255 turns on, 140 off ($61C3).
Set to keep the cursor off ($644A), in fire mode.
The address of the unit tiles' rows by kind: $C2C2.
The address of the unit tiles by what the unit holds and its facing: $C342.
The address of the falling bodies: $C37A.
The address of the scenario's messages: $C38A.
The address of the scenario's dictionary: $C510.
The address of the terrain types: $CBA8.
The address of the kinds of object: $CE60.
The address of the scenario's objects: $D068.
findRoute's stack pointer: the route so far, three bytes a waypoint from $5B01.
nextLink's link number in the list of the waypoint ZONE.
nextLink's list: the address of the links of the waypoint ZONE.
The waypoint whose links nextLink is reading.

From the waypoint ZONE, the links from the A-th on: the first to a waypoint not on the route so far (onPath) whose cost, added to the route's, is below BEST: Z, ZONE that waypoint, B the cost, LINK_I the link's number. NZ when the list ends (a byte with bit 7 set: each list begins with its length, with bit 7 set, so the next list's length ends this one).
Z if waypoint A is on the route so far (the 50 entries of three bytes from $5B01), or is 0.
findRoute's cost of the best route so far.
findRoute's depth: the waypoints on the route so far.

The cheapest route from waypoint FROM to waypoint TO, tried link by link, deepest first, with every route that gets there cheaper than the best so far kept: its waypoints, ten at most, at $5CF0, its cost in BEST (to begin with the distance between the two waypoints' areas, or 25 in the same area) and FOUND set. The route so far is a stack of three bytes a waypoint from $5B01: the waypoint, the link tried last, the cost to it. This copy keeps no flag of a route found: its callers compare the cost alone.
Two bytes after pointAt's RET, $00 $00, that no instruction refers to.
A = the number of the area the square ($5D3A) lies in, or 0 for none.
A = the cost between areas AREA_A and AREA_B (0 for the same): a triangle of bytes from DISTANCES, a row for each area from the second, as long as its number less one.
The cheapest route found so far to any waypoint next to the hunted enemy.
The action points a unit keeps in hand: half its most when its orders say so.

The computer's half-turn ($B621): the sides along the bottom and the view hidden, then each of its units on the map in turn ($5C50, side 1): $5D26 its number, $5D24 its square, $5D2F the square's place in the map, $5D33 and IX its record, ORDER its orders; selected, and its move. An empty weapon is simply given 60 rounds, and its clip too, in place of a reload. Units from $9C are aliens: they go for the terminals (alienMove).

The alien's move: an alien ($5D26 from $9C) shoots a terminal it can see (terminalAttack), or walks to the waypoint of the one it is after ($1A, chosen at random when it has none or that one is gone): with an enemy in sight it fires (peek) instead, an enemy known is faced; at the terminal's waypoint it chooses again in its next turn.

The unit's move, as its jumps go: with no rounds in its weapon ($24) it reloads when it carries a clip of the weapon's kind ($10); an enemy in sight is fired at (peek); then, while it can go on ($5D37 clear), an enemy known (knownEnemy) is faced and fired at from the square next to it nearest, else the enemy chosen is hunted (bit 3 of the orders' flags clear), else the orders walked. An alien does not hunt.
NZ, and $B713 the unit, when one of the enemies listed from $5B99 (by twos and threes: the game reads the list a byte out) has been seen lately (its count at $B63A + its number not 0).
The address of the moving unit's orders in ORDERS.
The unit's orders: the waypoint byte 0 picks (GOAL), back to the first after the last (a 0), made for (moveOn) and, when the unit is there, the next.
The waypoint the unit is making for.
Set when the unit reached GOAL.

Walk the unit to waypoint GOAL (or, hunting, on to the enemy TARGET once there): the route from the nearest waypoint it can see (findRoute), its first waypoint passed over when the second is in sight, then square by square (step) to each waypoint of it in turn; ARRIVED set at GOAL. Here a square whose step answer ($5D29) is 6 or more is opened or broken through like a door.

A step to ($5D3A), faced first (faceTo): made (makeStep), kept on the trail and the unit's panel shown, unless its points less RESERVE do not pay for it, or (bit 2 of the orders' flags, or hunting) an enemy that could still fire would see it there (aiDanger): then $5D37 is set and the unit stops. Here every step ends in terminalAttack, which acts only for aliens (units from $9C).
The address of the trail's end: the squares the unit stepped on in this walk.
Z if the square ($5D3A) is on the trail (25 squares from $5C0A, ended by $FF).
A new trail, TRAIL at its start.
faceTo's eighths of a turn to the left.
faceTo's eighths of a turn to the right.
Turn the unit to face the square ($5D3A) next to it, by the shorter way round, an eighth (and an action point) at a time; Z when it may not go on (aiCanGo), NZ when it faces it.
A = the number of the waypoint at the square HL (L the row), or 0 and Z.
A = the waypoint at the unit's square ($5D24), or the nearest to it of those it can see (NEAREST; its distance NEAR_D).
NZ while the unit has points beyond RESERVE (not exactly those) and lives, and no enemy is in sight; Z otherwise, with $5D37 set, or (an enemy in sight) $B714.
peek's cost of the step to cover, plus one (0 for none).

With enemies in sight. Of the eight squares round the unit ($A5CA, the steps), each is given the cost of a step onto it (the terrain's byte for the unit's kind, $04), or $FF when an enemy can be seen from it, a unit stands there or the unit cannot go there; the cheapest is COVER, its cost + 1 COVER_COST (0 for none). The unit fires (the hook at $B624, aiFire) and then, with enemies still in sight and a square of cover, is put on it, with no points left.

The computer's reaction ($B624): with rounds in its weapon, the unit aims at one of the enemies in sight ($5CA0, one of $5D59 at random) when the line to it is clear, the map as the computer sees it; its shot by the range (RANGES: aimed from the first on, snap from the second, auto below) and its points, keeping COVER_COST for the step to cover after; again while enemies are in sight and it lives. $5D37 set when it cannot.
The view's corner at the enemy's square (DE), the crosshair 5 to 10 pixels into it across and down, at random.

TARGET, the enemy that scores the most (SCORE), listed with its score from $5B00: its $27, plus a value for each object it carries (KIND_VALUES), plus the value of the area it stands in for the unit's orders (VALUES, row $09 of the orders, 0 leaves the enemy out), plus half of 255 less the cost to its area, plus how long it will be remembered ($B63A), each sum at most 255. An enemy in no area scores 0. This copy leaves IX on the record of the last unit it scored. This copy has no values for the areas: where an enemy stands adds only the cost to it.
DE = unit A's square, from the table at $5C50.
The waypoints that can be seen from the square ($5D3A), listed from $5C0A ($5D8F of them): the waypoint on the square itself first, if there is one.

The hook at $B627, a shot's square HL: when an enemy of the side firing can see it, the unit firing ($5D26) is remembered by the computer ($B63A + its number = its skill, $5DF8) and $B714 set. The line's start ($7091, $7093) is put back.

NZ when, from the square ($5D3A) the unit is to step to, an enemy it remembers ($B63A) could see it (inView) with more than half the points it starts a turn with left. Here the half is of the enemy's most action points, less one, and units from $9C fear nothing.
The hook at $B62A: in the computer's turn the view is blanked (tile 0 in black, 11 squares by 11) and message $65 shown, once ($B715).
The values chooseTarget adds to an enemy's score for each object it carries, a byte for each kind from $6E: ; the rest 0.
The ranges of aiFire's shots: aimed from 14 squares away, auto shots under 6, snap shots between.
